As Connecticut does not have gubernatorial term limits, incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governor [[Dannel Malloy]] was eligible to run for a third term, but declined to do so. After the resignation of Kansas governor [[Sam Brownback]] in January 2018, Malloy became the most unpopular governor in the United States.{{cite web |url=http://nymag.com/daily/intelligencer/2018/08/connecticut-governor-gamin-lamont-2018.html |title=Establishment vs. Ex-con in Connecticut Democrats's Gubernatorial Primary |work=[[New York (magazine)|New York]] |author=David Freedlander |date=August 13, 2018 |access-date=August 13, 2018}}{{Cite web |url=https://morningconsult.com/state-governor-rankings/ |title=News and Analysis |access-date=August 15, 2018 |archive-date=May 1, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180501103923/https://morningconsult.com/state-governor-rankings/ |url-status=dead }} The general election was between [[2006 United States Senate election in Connecticut|2006]] Democratic U.S. Senate nominee [[Ned Lamont]], and Republican financial executive [[Bob Stefanowski]]. Independent candidate and former Republican [[Oz Griebel]] has been called a [[spoiler effect|spoiler candidate]] for Stefanowski, earning 3.89% of the vote.{{Cite web |
